evals.name: loki-on-flux-with-eso
evals.prompt: I want to add Loki for log aggregation to our cluster. The GitOps repo for our infrastructure is at <FIXTURE_PATH>. Please configure persistence with a 50Gi PVC.
evals.expected_output: FluxCD manifests (HelmRepository + HelmRelease + Kustomization + namespace) for Loki, written under infra/loki/ to match the existing Pattern D layout. No ExternalSecret needed (Loki with filesystem storage). Persistence configured at 50Gi.

assertions.name: picked_flux
assertions.text: Generated manifests use FluxCD (kind: HelmRelease), not ArgoCD

assertions.name: pattern_d_layout
assertions.text: Files written under infra/loki/ to match Pattern D component-based layout

assertions.name: kustomization_present
assertions.text: kustomization.yaml present in the new loki directory

assertions.name: helmrepository_present
assertions.text: HelmRepository resource generated

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned
assertions.text: HelmRelease chart.spec.version is a specific pinned version

assertions.name: chart_version_current
assertions.text: Chart version is current (Loki forked to grafana-community in Mar 2026; current is 14.x community / 7.x grafana)

assertions.name: persistence_50gi
assertions.text: Loki persistence configured at 50Gi as the user explicitly requested

assertions.name: no_unneeded_externalsecret
assertions.text: No unnecessary ExternalSecret generated (filesystem-mode Loki needs none)

assertions.name: namespace_present
assertions.text: namespace.yaml generated for the new loki namespace

evals.name: cert-manager-argocd-cloudflare-dns01
evals.prompt: Set up cert-manager in our cluster with Cloudflare DNS01 challenges for ACME so we can get wildcard certificates. Our GitOps repo is at <FIXTURE_PATH>. We use Cloudflare as our DNS provider.
evals.expected_output: ArgoCD Application for cert-manager under argocd/apps/. ClusterIssuer with Cloudflare DNS01 solver referencing a Kubernetes Secret. Cloudflare Secret (if generated) is a placeholder template with a warning, not a real token.

assertions.name: picked_argocd
assertions.text: Generated manifests use ArgoCD (kind: Application), not Flux

assertions.name: argocd_apps_path
assertions.text: cert-manager Application placed under argocd/apps/ to match existing convention

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned
assertions.text: Application's targetRevision is a specific pinned chart version

assertions.name: chart_version_current
assertions.text: cert-manager chart version is current (within ~2 minors of v1.20.2 as of May 2026)

assertions.name: cloudflare_dns01_clusterissuer
assertions.text: ClusterIssuer/Issuer generated with Cloudflare DNS01 solver

assertions.name: cloudflare_token_via_secret
assertions.text: Cloudflare API token referenced via Secret (apiTokenSecretRef), not plaintext

assertions.name: cloudflare_secret_is_placeholder
assertions.text: Cloudflare API token Secret (if generated) contains a placeholder + warning, not a real-looking token

assertions.name: crd_install_handled
assertions.text: CRDs handled (installCRDs:true or ServerSideApply=true)

evals.name: greenfield-prometheus-grafana
evals.prompt: I need to set up Prometheus and Grafana to monitor my cluster. We're just getting started with GitOps. Repo path: <FIXTURE_PATH>.
evals.expected_output: Combined kube-prometheus-stack chart (not two separate charts) in a component directory under infra/ or infrastructure/. Pinned version. Manifests use one tool's CRDs (no mixing).

assertions.name: uses_kube_prometheus_stack
assertions.text: Output uses combined kube-prometheus-stack chart, NOT two separate Prometheus and Grafana charts

assertions.name: pattern_d_recommended
assertions.text: Output structure groups manifests in a component directory under infra/ or infrastructure/

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned
assertions.text: Chart version pinned to a specific release

assertions.name: chart_version_current
assertions.text: kube-prometheus-stack chart version is current (within ~5 minors of 85.x as of May 2026)

assertions.name: manifests_match_chosen_tool
assertions.text: Generated manifests use the right CRDs for the chosen tool (no mixing)

assertions.name: no_unrequested_grafana_creds
assertions.text: No unrequested Grafana credential resources (placeholder Secret, inline adminPassword, or existingSecret reference) — chart auto-generates admin Secret on install and user did not ask for credential management

evals.name: loki-s3-backend-secret-required
evals.prompt: I want to add Loki for log aggregation, configured with S3-backed storage so we can keep logs long-term. The bucket is my-logs-2026 in us-east-1. Our GitOps repo is at <FIXTURE_PATH>.
evals.expected_output: FluxCD HelmRelease for Loki configured with S3 storage backend (bucket my-logs-2026, region us-east-1), under infra/loki/. Since S3 access requires AWS credentials the user must supply AND the fixture has ESO installed, the skill should generate an ExternalSecret referencing the existing ClusterSecretStore — not a placeholder native Secret. AWS credentials must never be inlined in HelmRelease values.

assertions.name: picked_flux
assertions.text: Generated manifests use FluxCD (kind: HelmRelease), not ArgoCD

assertions.name: pattern_d_layout
assertions.text: Files written under infra/loki/ (Pattern D component-based layout)

assertions.name: loki_s3_backend_configured
assertions.text: Loki HelmRelease values configure S3 storage backend (bucket my-logs-2026 referenced, region us-east-1)

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned_current
assertions.text: Loki chart version is pinned to a current release (grafana-community 14.x or grafana 7.x as of May 2026)

assertions.name: secret_resource_generated
assertions.text: Some Secret/ExternalSecret/SealedSecret resource is generated for AWS credentials (chart REQUIRES creds when S3 backend is enabled — case 1 of the anti-anticipation rule)

assertions.name: prefers_eso_when_available
assertions.text: Generated secret resource is an ExternalSecret referencing the existing ClusterSecretStore (since ESO is detected in the fixture repo)

assertions.name: no_inline_aws_creds
assertions.text: AWS access key / secret access key are NOT inlined into HelmRelease values — must come from a Secret reference

evals.name: postgresql-with-explicit-auth
evals.prompt: Deploy PostgreSQL for our backend service. We need to manage the database password via a Kubernetes Secret so we can rotate it later. Database name should be appdb, username appuser. Our GitOps repo is at <FIXTURE_PATH>.
evals.expected_output: FluxCD HelmRelease for PostgreSQL under infra/postgresql/ (or similar Pattern D dir) with auth.existingSecret reference (NOT inlined auth.password). Database name 'appdb' and username 'appuser' configured in HelmRelease values. Since the fixture has ESO installed and the user explicitly wants Secret-managed credentials, an ExternalSecret should be generated.

assertions.name: picked_flux
assertions.text: Generated manifests use FluxCD (kind: HelmRelease)

assertions.name: pattern_d_layout
assertions.text: Files under infra/<postgres-dir>/ (Pattern D)

assertions.name: uses_existing_secret_pattern
assertions.text: HelmRelease wires auth.existingSecret (or similar) — does NOT inline auth.password directly

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned
assertions.text: PostgreSQL chart version is pinned

assertions.name: secret_resource_generated
assertions.text: Some Secret/ExternalSecret/SealedSecret resource is generated (user EXPLICITLY requested Kubernetes-Secret-managed credentials)

assertions.name: prefers_eso_when_available
assertions.text: Generated secret resource is an ExternalSecret (since ESO is detected in the fixture repo)

assertions.name: db_name_and_user_configured
assertions.text: Database name 'appdb' and username 'appuser' appear in HelmRelease values

assertions.name: no_inline_password
assertions.text: auth.password (or password key) is NOT inlined with a placeholder value like 'changeme' in HelmRelease values

evals.name: externaldns-route53-needs-aws-creds
evals.prompt: Deploy ExternalDNS to manage Route53 records for our cluster. We're on AWS but NOT using IRSA. Domain to manage: example.com. Our GitOps repo is at <FIXTURE_PATH>.
evals.expected_output: ArgoCD Application for ExternalDNS in argocd/apps/. ExternalDNS values configured with provider: aws and a domainFilter for example.com. Since the user is not using IRSA (so credentials must be supplied) AND the fixture has no secrets backend, a native Kubernetes Secret with placeholder values for AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY should be generated with a clear warning header. AWS credentials must never be inlined into the helm.values block.

assertions.name: picked_argocd
assertions.text: Generated manifests use ArgoCD (kind: Application), not Flux

assertions.name: argocd_apps_path
assertions.text: ExternalDNS Application placed under argocd/apps/

assertions.name: externaldns_aws_provider
assertions.text: ExternalDNS values configure provider: aws

assertions.name: externaldns_domain_filter
assertions.text: domainFilter (or similar) references example.com

assertions.name: chart_version_pinned
assertions.text: ExternalDNS chart's targetRevision is pinned

assertions.name: secret_resource_generated
assertions.text: A Secret resource is generated for AWS credentials (user not on IRSA; chart REQUIRES creds — case 1 of the anti-anticipation rule)

assertions.name: secret_is_placeholder
assertions.text: Generated Secret contains placeholder values (REPLACE_THIS, CHANGEME, etc) and a warning header — never a real-looking AWS key

assertions.name: no_inline_aws_creds
assertions.text: AWS access key / secret access key are NOT inlined directly into the helm.values block
